ranking.note: Raised: seed generation is the top-listed deployment-facing tool here, and an abandoned/hijackable source feeding hardcoded release seeds is an integrity problem, not cleanup.
Raised and moved up seven places: measurable snapshot-load speedup plus a new bitcoin-util txoutsetsummary tool, and #35054 builds on it, so it outranks the purely developer-convenience P3s.
Raised: the new bitcoin-privbcast utility exists to close recurring deanonymization/privacy leaks, which outweighs the ordinary new-tool P3s even though the surrounding change is large.
Raised from P4: silently swallowing trailing options and misrouting -rpcwallet is a correctness defect across bitcoin-cli, bitcoin-wallet and bitcoin-tx, comparable to the other P3 tool fixes.

inconsistencies: Chain: #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect) sits on #10102 and #29409 and is itself the prerequisite for #19461; reviewing it before its dependencies land will mostly re-litigate them.

Chain: #36190 is a test follow-up to the already-merged wrapper fixes in #36105 and overlaps the wrapper behaviour touched by #36106; review #36106 first so the tests are written against the final path-resolution logic.

#35814 is the fourth attempt at issue #17289 after #18606, #25243 and #30860 stalled, and now depends on merged OpenRPC support (#34683); a reviewer should confirm the earlier attempts are closed rather than competing.

#36603 and #36608 both land new bitcoin-util/standalone binaries while mostly changing node-side code; their tool surface is the part in scope for this category, and the band here reflects only that plus the downstream work (#35054) they unblock.
#35994 is self-superseded: the author states a preference for abandoning it in favour of manual rewrites, so review time spent on the clang-tidy check is likely wasted regardless of band.
result.notes: Only one PR in this list has release-security consequence (#36293); the rest split cleanly into deployment-facing tool fixes (wrapper, seeds, snapshot tooling, private broadcast) and developer-convenience tools. I kept that split rather than flattening everything into P3, which is where most cards individually landed.
